title: Dapple and the Silent Snow-Chime
markdown:
The Highland country glittered, and the village snow-chime—a wonder of crystal and harps—had fallen silent. Its joyous song was gone. It fell to Dapple, a goblin known more for muddy knees than brilliance, to mend the hush.

“Magic, Dapple! That’s what’s needed!” Elder Bramble’s beard was frosted white. “The chime must sing again. The village depends on it.”

Dapple, small, ears twitching, scratched one. “But Elder, I think a really strong gust, guided just right, might do it.”

Pickle, a rat with twitching whiskers, squeaked agreement from Dapple’s shoulder.

From the shimmering mist, Moss the elf huffed, fingers dripping stardust. “A gust of wind? Primitive, my dear Dapple. This calls for ethereal enchantment.”

Dapple shrugged. “It might work, Moss. And it won’t turn anyone green.”

Moss sniffed, a snowflake melting, and returned to his spellcasting.

Dapple and Pickle set off toward the highest peaks, the silent chime at their backs like a held breath. On a narrow path a vast shadow fell: Gruff, the ogre shepherd. “Hullo, little goblin. Off to fix the chime? Heard it’s gone quiet. Shame.”

A thumb the size of a boulder. “Wind’s been blowing from the north-east. Always does this time of year. But this ridge—” brow furrowing—“it’s been pushed out, angled just so, as if to catch the wind and send it sailing.”

Dapple’s eyes widened. Pickle squeaked. The lumbering ogre had noticed something. Dapple looked at the ridge, the wind, his simple sensible idea.

“Thank you, Gruff. That’s just what I needed.”

Moss, meanwhile, had accidentally turned his entire grove of moonpetal flowers a rather alarming indigo, complete with purple polka dots. He sighed, wondering if Dapple’s silly wind-based notion had any merit after all.

Dapple and Pickle scrambled up the angled ridge. With goblin energy and clever knots, Dapple lashed sturdy wind-bent branches into a giant rustic fan. He positioned it to funnel the north-easterly straight at the silent snow-chime.

A deep breath. He nudged the wind-catcher into place. The wind surged, caught, and went whistling at the chime’s heart.

The crystal harps sang. Ice crystals chimed, a melody so pure it ran the valleys and chased the heavy silence. A thousand tiny silver bells set free.

Moss arrived trailing wilting indigo petals. He stopped dead. The chime sang, clear and true, without a speck of stardust. “But—how?” He stared at the simple catcher.

Dapple beamed, dusting his hands. “Just a strong wind, Moss. And a good angle.”

Gruff ambled up, a happy rumbling chuckle. “See? Told you that ridge was up to something. Clever little goblin.”

Moss looked from singing chime to Dapple, a new respect. “Perhaps there is a different kind of magic in practicality.”

Villagers gathered, not in silence now but in listening. Pickle washed his whiskers as if he had planned the knots all along. The snow-chime kept the tune, and Dapple’s muddy knees, for once, were the least interesting thing about him.
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing mountain adventure fantasy for ages 9-10
